open_questions.question: Which agents can be watched? Answer (operator, 2026-11-15): every agent, including this agent's other conversations.
Default conversation and following? Answer (operator, 2026-11-15): the running one, else most recent; follow the agent unless picked by hand.
State shown? Answer (operator, 2026-11-15): working, idle and waiting for your answer.

Remembered per what? Answer (operator, 2026-11-15): per project, after the earlier 'per conversation, like the other tabs' was found to rest on a wrong premise (open tabs are kept per project, panelTabsStore.ts:1-4; vault fact fct-ca14ea7023c0). The not-twice rule follows from it.

problem: With several agents building at once (a flow hands tasks to four or five), the operator talking to one of them cannot see what another is doing without leaving the conversation they are in, losing their place and their unsent draft. The roadmap's last slice (peer-conversation) answers this. Grounding, master 405bef8: a presentational WatchTab exists (hub/ui/src/components/panel/WatchTab.tsx) but only the mock uses it (hub/ui/mock/screens/SidePanel.tsx:178-200); the panel's tab ids stop at specs/files/running/changes/terminal (hub/ui/src/store/panelTabsStore.ts:31), and which tabs are open is kept per project (panelTabsStore.ts:1-4). The data is already there: the browser's single event stream carries every conversation's agent_output, filtered per hook (hub/ui/src/api/agentChat.ts:348-359, :426), and useAgentChatHistory(agent, conversation) plus the read-only AgentTimeline (components/agents/AgentTimeline.tsx:32-60) draw any conversation. Working state is AgentSummary.running_conversation_id (api/agents.ts:15-29); open questions carry their agent and conversation (api/questions.ts:60, hub/hub/api/v1/questions.py:164-197), so 'waiting for your answer' needs no Hub change.

requirements.statement: The conversation side panel offers a Watch tab alongside Specs, Files, Running, Changes and Terminal, opened, closed and remembered like the others (which tabs are open is kept per project).

requirements.rationale: A flow runs the same agent in several conversations, so watching only other agents would miss the case the operator asked for (operator, 2026-11-15).
requirements.statement: The Watch tab's agent menu lists every agent of the current project, including the conversation's own agent, each with its colour and what it is doing now; its conversation menu lists the chosen agent's open conversations, newest activity first.

requirements.rationale: With what is watched kept per project, the main view can arrive at the watched conversation; two copies of one timeline side by side add nothing.
requirements.statement: When the watched conversation is the one shown in the main view, the Watch tab does not draw it a second time: it says the operator is in this conversation and offers the watched agent's other conversations; watching resumes when the main view moves elsewhere.

Choosing an agent opens the conversation it is running now, or its most recently active conversation when it is idle; an agent with no conversation shows that it has none yet rather than an empty timeline.

requirements.rationale: Following keeps the tab live as a flow moves the agent from task to task; a hand pick is a deliberate choice that must not be taken away mid-read.
requirements.statement: While the operator has not picked a conversation by hand, the tab switches to the conversation the watched agent starts running next; once the operator picks one by hand, it stays on that conversation until they choose an agent again.

requirements.rationale: Watch only (roadmap, operator 2026-11-12): two composers side by side make it easy to write to the wrong agent.
requirements.statement: The watched conversation is drawn as the main view draws it (messages, turn output, tool calls) and new output appears as the agent produces it without a reload; the tab offers no way to send a message, answer a question, stop a run or change the queue.

requirements.rationale: Waiting for an answer is the state the operator most needs to see (operator, 2026-11-15).
requirements.statement: The tab says whether the watched agent is working, idle, or waiting for the operator's answer, the last whenever the agent has an unanswered question, and the statement changes when that state does without a reload.

requirements.rationale: The tab's purpose is keeping an eye on one agent while talking to several; it matches the panel's other per-project state (operator, 2026-11-15).
requirements.statement: The watched agent and conversation are kept per project: switching the main view to any other conversation of the project, or reloading the page, leaves the Watch tab showing the same agent and conversation; a remembered conversation that has since been closed falls back to the default conversation of that agent, and a remembered agent that no longer exists leaves the tab asking which agent to watch.
The tab has a control that makes the watched conversation the main view in one click, where the operator can talk to that agent; the conversation they left keeps its unsent draft.

in_scope: A Watch tab in the conversation side panel
Choosing which agent, and which of its conversations, to watch, including this agent's other conversations
The watched conversation drawn as the main view draws it, updating live, read-only
Saying whether the watched agent is working, idle or waiting for the operator's answer
Following the agent into a new conversation unless the operator picked one by hand
Remembering what is watched per project, across switching conversations and reload
One click to make the watched conversation the main view
non_goals: Sending messages, answering questions, stopping runs or managing the queue from the Watch tab (roadmap: watch only)
Watching several conversations at once in split views
Watching an agent of another project
Notifications or sounds for events in the watched conversation
Any Hub route or migration: the slice uses data the browser already receives
Changing how the panel remembers which tabs are open: that stays per project
A different watched agent per main-view conversation (operator, 2026-11-15: per project)

summary: While talking to one agent, the operator opens a Watch tab in the side panel, picks another agent (or another conversation of the same agent), and sees that conversation stream in live and read-only, with what the agent is doing now — working, idle or waiting for the operator's answer — and one click to switch the main view to it. What is watched is kept per project, so it stays put as the operator moves between conversations.
